questions.question: What is an acceptable oil pressure when an engine is running?
questions.correctAnswerText: 50 psi.
questions.explanation: Good oil pressure is between 35 and 75 psi. Do not drive if your oil pressure is low, dropping, or unsteady.

questions.question: Driving combination vehicles usually requires ____ skill than driving single vehicles.
questions.correctAnswerText: More
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles. They need more skill to drive safely.

questions.question: If you stop on the side of the road, what must you do within 10 minutes?
questions.correctAnswerText: Place emergency warning devices.
questions.explanation: You must place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the side of the road.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how do you know the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start the engine, the lights should come on and then turn off. If the yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on, the ABS is not working properly.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: Stay on the shoulder until you stop. Then signal, check your mirrors, and merge back into traffic. Do not brake hard at high speeds on the shoulder. Try to keep one set of wheels on the pavement.

questions.question: How should you brake if your ABS is not working?

options.text: Brake normally, as you will still have regular brakes.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally, as you will still have regular brakes.
questions.explanation: Without ABS, your vehicle still has normal brakes. Drive and brake as usual. Get your ABS fixed as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should you do with wheel rims that have been welded?

options.text: Use them on the rear wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use them.
questions.explanation: Welded wheels or rims are not safe and should not be used.

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) do?

options.text: They are not used on trucks.
They are only used on trucks carrying hazardous materials.
They help drivers stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help drivers stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents wheels from locking up when you brake hard. This helps you keep control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which sign shows that cargo contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is from a supermarket.
The cargo is in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold hazardous materials. The type of packaging is a clue about what you are carrying.

questions.question: Why should you check tires often in very hot weather?

options.text: The tread wears down faster than in cool weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure increases with temperature.
questions.explanation: Hot weather raises air pressure in tires. Pay close attention to tire pressure and how your tires are mounted when driving in hot weather.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail while driving downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Let rumble strips slow your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer onto an escape ramp.
questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, use an escape ramp to stop. An escape ramp is the best option. If no escape ramp is available, drive into an open field or side road that goes uphill or flattens out.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: When driving a tank vehicle, a driver should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase their following distance.
questions.explanation: Liquid in tanks can shift and surge. Start braking well before you need to stop. Keep more distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts can mean the nuts are loose. If you see rust near the wheel nuts, check that they are tight before driving.

questions.question: In a leaf spring:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leaves should not be broken.
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs do not have missing or broken leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle cannot be driven until it is fixed.

questions.question: A manifest for transporting hazardous waste:

options.text: Must be attached to the outside of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must be signed by hand.
questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. It must be signed by hand.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, your vehicle should not be:

options.text: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
Parked within 40 feet of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parked within 300 feet of a bridge.
questions.explanation: Never park a vehicle carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, or building. Only park briefly for necessary vehicle operations like refueling. Never park within five feet of the road.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
A valve that prevents a truck from being stolen.
A valve that prevents the driver from driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or has a bad leak. The valve closes automatically if air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When inspecting the windshield before a trip, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
Check the windshield wipers for proper spring tension.
Check the wiper blades for damage.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove and sharpen the wiper blades.
questions.explanation: When inspecting your windshield, look for cracks or damage that could block your view. Check the wiper arms for proper spring tension. Check the wiper blades for damage, stiff rubber, and to make sure they are secure.

questions.question: If you stay in neutral too long while switching gears:

options.text: You may have trouble putting the vehicle into the next gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have trouble putting the vehicle into the next gear.
questions.explanation: If you stay in neutral too long while switching gears, you may have trouble putting the vehicle into the next gear. Do not force the gear shift. Instead, return to neutral, release the clutch, increase engine speed to match road speed, and try again.
